I reported six findings on the four new functions in `fees.py`. Four are correctness bugs, one is missing tests, and one is duplicated code. I only read the diff; I didn't run the code or write any tests.

- **`average_fee`:** It divides by `len(payments)` with no empty check. An empty list raises `ZeroDivisionError`, although the docstring says it returns 0.
- **`paginate`:** It uses `start = page * size`, but `page` is documented as 1-based. Page 1 returns items 10–19, so the first page can't be reached.
- **`dedupe_members`:** It keys on `m["name"]`, while the docstring says identity is decided by email. Two different people with the same name get merged, and one is dropped.
- **`unpaid_members`:** It compares emails exactly, so `A@x.com` and `a@x.com` don't match. A member who paid can be listed as unpaid.
- **Tests:** None of the new functions have tests.
- **Duplication:** `average_fee` repeats the sum from `total_fee`.

I couldn't read `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` because the tool blocked reading outside the working directory. The repo has no `CLAUDE.md`, so I made no conventions finding.
